newsitem.title: UK: Higher bid for Northern Electric seen.
newsitem.headline: Higher bid for Northern Electric seen.

text.p: Shares in Northern Electric added to earlier gains, rising 116-1/2 pence to 636-1/2 on the day amid expectations that predator CalEnergy would raise its offer to win backing from Northern's board.

Philip Hollobone, analyst at Williams de Broe, said he expected CalEnergy to lift its offer to somewhere between 650 and 657 pence per share from the current 630 pence. "We will see an agreed bid eventually," he said.
But Andrew Stone at Daiwa said CalEnergy would have good reasons not to raise its offer to the same levels as last year's bids for other regional electricity firms.
"The company (Northern) has paid out a couple of special dividends and is very highly geared, which has to be taken into account," Stone said.

Last year's bids in the electricity sector were made at levels of around 14 times earnings, while the offer -- made by CalEnergy through its 70 percent owned unit CE Electric -- values Northern at a price to earnings ratio of about 10.5.
"There might well be some upside, but I don't think we're likely to see the 14 times earnings figure," said Stone.

Northern Electric successfully fought off an offer from Trafalgar House last year by paying special dividends. But as a result the company's balance sheet is too weak now to squeeze a substantially higher bid out of CalEnergy, Hollobone said.
The U.S. firm said it had been in talks with Northern Electric, which disagreed on the price, but had no other objections.
